_meta.purpose: Pattern subset of the notation contract, read by verify_paper9.py.

_meta.note: The patterns necessarily quote the internal labels they prohibit — that is the mechanism of the check, not a violation of it. No other field of the working contract is published.

forbidden_patterns.reason: Unimodular constant must be \omega_0, never \zeta (clash with zeta(s)); kanon_lemma v1.1+.
Internal sprint/program names never appear in papers (Terminologie-Mapping, Paper9_Konzeptnotiz).
B = sum (log p)^2 Re(Z_p) is WRONG. Must be Re(Z_p^{(2)}). (Pattern sharpened in review cycle to avoid false positives on B_int.)
Use \varepsilon, never \epsilon.
Internal project labels must not appear in papers.
SAA (Subleading Archimedean Assumption) is an internal project abbreviation. Use 'Assumption~\ref{ass:subleading}' or 'a subleading archimedean condition' in published papers.
PT (Proxy Transfer) is an internal project abbreviation. Use 'Assumption~\ref{ass:proxy}' or 'a proxy-transfer condition' in published papers.
Use 'non-circular and proof-complete' instead.
Big-O in NUMERICAL theorems is overclaim. Use 'consistent with linear scaling'.
In NUMERICAL context, use 'appears to converge (numerical extrapolation)'.
r_p^infty = 1/2 universally (review cycle). Values 0.5, 0.6, 0.75, 0.8 etc. are finite-eps artifacts. Use exactly 1/2 in analytic statements.
Pole contribution h(i/2)+h(-i/2) = 2 e^{eps^2/4} cosh(log p/2). Use cosh, never cos.
GW convention requires hat g(u) = (1/(2pi)) int h(t) e^{-iut} dt (Iwaniec-Kowalski form, established review cycle).

Sign convention error: O'(1/2) = +2.4751 at reference parameters (kappa=53, eps=0.05, N=100). The historical value -2.475 was a sign artifact (review cycle May 2026 correction). Magnitudes identical, sign positive with O(sigma) = (1/2) sum exp(-eps^2 gamma_k^2) cos(2 sigma gamma_k log p).
Internal lemma labels L1..L6 must not appear as standalone tokens in published papers. Use neutral mathematical labels (e.g., 'Lemma A', 'Theorem 4.1').
Internal open-finding labels (OF-EXPLICIT-1, OF-CONST-1, etc.) are sprint-internal. Use neutral references in papers.

rank(T_tilde) = ... = pi(kappa) chains an unproven equality (rank(Phi) = pi(kappa) requires linear independence of {a_p}). Either weaken to 'at most pi(kappa)' or cite an independence lemma. (HIGH 5 catch.)
rank(...) = pi(kappa) without an independence lemma is HIGH 5. Use 'at most pi(kappa)' or cite independence.

Bare c_p is ambiguous and is forbidden here. In the eta framework use c_p^eta := sqrt(V_p(1/2)) (Paper 3); in the Weil-renormalised framework use c_p^ren := sqrt(f_p) (Paper 4, Paper 9). The two weights are distinct and must never be identified. V_p(1/2) = f_p + 4(log p)^2/p.

A** asks only for a logarithmic saving in the ordinate aspect relative to the trivial P(kappa) bound; that compares demanded cancellation strength (log-saving vs sqrt-saving), it is NOT a logical implication. A** is neither equivalent to RH nor known to follow from RH (Paper 7 v0.17, Non-Circularity). Equivalence claim is FALSE. review cycle Stat-II (May 2026).
A** must use P(kappa) (Chebyshev theta), NOT pi(kappa). review cycle Stat-II (May 2026) corrected this from the original startprompt: |M_k|/pi grows with kappa, |M_k|/P stays bounded.
Theorem Stat-II is CONDITIONAL under A**, never UNCONDITIONAL. review cycle (FAIL) tried UNCONDITIONAL via Pole-vs-Zero error; review cycle Stat-II strictly CONDITIONAL.

O''(1/2) > 0 is an ASYMPTOTIC consequence (eps -> 0 at fixed kappa) of B < 0 (OF-CONST-1, internal). NOT uniform for finite (kappa, eps). review cycle (May 2026) documented 7 sign-failures. Universal claim is FALSE.

O''(½) > 0 ist eine ASYMPTOTISCHE Konsequenz (ε → 0 bei festem κ) aus B < 0 (OF-CONST-1, intern). NICHT uniform für endliche (κ, ε). review cycle (Mai 2026) dokumentiert 7 Sign-Failures. Universal-Aussage ist FALSCH.

B < 0 is an ASYMPTOTIC statement (eps -> 0 at fixed kappa, OF-CONST-1 internal). NOT uniform for finite (kappa, eps). review cycle (May 2026) found B > 0 at (kappa in {2003, 5003}, eps >= 0.075). Universal claim is FALSE.
